turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: For me, it's hard to describe, but I personally now can pretty cleanly tell the difference between exhaustion and depression. And it tends to tie to my broader motivations, not just my motivation to work. So, when I'm exhausted, I'll still show up to work, I'll still execute, I'll still do those types of things, but I'm going to go and if I can take an improv class, it's going to be a blast. I'm going to enjoy it and I'm going to love it. If I'm depressed, I won't go to that improv class. I'll just cancel it. I won't go to it. Or if I go to it, I'll go home immediately. One of the things I love about actual improv classes, is the community. Is, "Hey, let's all go grab a drink now." And this is a totally different group of people. It's not my family, it's not my work people, it's just me.
turns.zh: 对我，难描述，但我个人现在能挺干净地区分 exhaustion 和抑郁。而且它倾向连到我更广的动机，不只是工作的动机。所以当我 exhaustion，我还会去工作、还会执行、还会做那些，但我会去、如果我能上个 improv 课，那会超好玩。我会享受、会爱它。如果我 depressed，我不会去那个 improv 课。我会直接取消。我不会去。或者如果我去了，我会立刻回家。真正的 improv 课我爱的一点，是社区。是「嘿，我们现在都去喝一杯。」而这是完全不同的另一群人。不是我家人、不是我工作的人，就是我。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: And I wouldn't do that. And so it's kind of noticing where else is this impacting and to what degree and why, can help me understand what's going on in my life. Because more often than not, I can then take those feelings and it'll be like, "Oh, I've felt this way for three weeks now. I should think about this and dissect it a little bit." And so again, I'll spend time with my therapist. One of the tools that my therapist has given me is to open up with my friends and have these conversations with my friends. And so now I went from five, six years ago really just having my therapist or my wife to talk about this kind of stuff to, I don't know, I have five or six different friends that we're massively transparent with each other about this stuff, because the second I shared any of this with them, they shared it with me.
turns.zh: 而我不会做那个。所以有点注意这还影响哪、到什么程度、为啥，能帮我理解我人生在发生什么。因为更多时候，我能然后拿那些感觉、会像「哦，我这感觉三周了。我该想这个、解剖一点。」所以再说一遍，我会花时间跟我的 therapist。我 therapist 给我的一个工具是向我朋友敞开、跟朋友有这些对话。所以现在我从五六年前的真的只有 therapist 或老婆聊这类事，到，我不知道，我有五六个不同朋友我们彼此极度透明聊这类事，因为我一跟他们分享任何这个，他们就跟我分享了。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: And now we've become safe places to have those conversations where I can be like, "Hey, there's this thing going on." My dad has ALS and so he's been really sick and I've got three kids and I've got jobs and work and money and the market crash. And there's so many different things. It's like, okay, let me actually figure out which one of these things is causing this energy right now. And having many years of therapy now and those resources can help me get to that solution to get to that answer so that I can figure out, okay, what do I need to do right now? Do I need to actually take time for myself and dig deeper into these personal things? Do I actually need to change something with the shape of my career? Those types of things.
turns.zh: 而现在我们对那些对话成了安全的地方，我能像「嘿，有这事在发生。」我爸有 ALS，所以他一直很病，我有三个孩子、我有工作、钱、市场崩。有这么多不同事。就像，好，让我真搞清楚这些事里哪个在造成这能量现在。而有多年 therapy 现在和那些资源能帮我到那个解、到那个答案，这样我能搞清楚，好，我现在需要做什么？我需要真给自己时间、深挖这些个人的事？我需要真改我职业生涯的形状？那些。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. And it sounds like the things that have been most helpful, and I'm curious what else you'd recommend to folks that are maybe feeling some of this. So, it sounds like therapy is really powerful, your partner and being open to your partner, finding a group of friends where you could be transparent about these sorts of things. Is there anything else you suggest folks look into?
turns.zh: 太棒了。听起来最有帮助的，我好奇你还推荐什么给也许感觉到一些这个的人。所以听起来 therapy 真的有力、你的伴侣和对伴侣敞开、找一群能对这些事透明的朋友。还有别的你建议人看吗？

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Yeah. So, I think meditation's a good one. The startup people love to talk about meditation, and so you can find lots of ways to do that. It's kind of evolved for me. So, it's in that tweet thread and I can't remember it now. There was a meditation thing that was the first, it almost felt like Noom for me for meditation where it wasn't just-
turns.zh: 对。我觉得冥想是个好的。创业的人爱聊冥想，所以你能找很多方式做。它对我演化了。在那时推文串里、我现在不记得。有个冥想的东西是第一个，它几乎对我像冥想的 Noom——不只是——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Waking Up, Sam Harris's-
turns.zh: Waking Up，Sam Harris 的——

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Yeah, Waking Up where it's like I'm actually learning about meditation, not just learning how to meditate. And that's how my brain likes to do things. I'm a lifetime learner, I love digging into things. I learned breathing techniques and things like that, but going through that program of Waking Up was the first time I actually really appreciated when and how and where to do it. I'm still not a everyday meditate person.
turns.zh: 对，Waking Up，像我是真在学关于冥想、不只是学怎么冥想。而那是我脑子喜欢做的方式。我是终身学习的人，爱深挖东西。我学了呼吸技巧那些，但过 Waking Up 那个项目是我第一次真欣赏什么时候、怎么、哪做它。我还不是每天冥想的人。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: I now use, I'm an investor, so I'm biased, but Aura, A-U-R-A, which is a marketplace app. It's some of the other meditation apps, but it's a marketplace, so it's actually coaches and stuff adding content. So, I use that now as needed, which I really enjoy. The exercise and diet and those types of things definitely tie to it. It's like eating is a pretty clean signal for me, or snacking is a really clean signal, at least for me of like, okay, I'm snacking more than I should be, and eating healthy can both help me identify that I'm in those spots, but also just make me feel better.
turns.zh: 我现在用，我是投资人，所以我有偏见，但 Aura，A-U-R-A，是个 marketplace app。它是别的冥想 app 一些，但它是 marketplace，所以其实是教练之类加内容。所以我按需用那个，我真的很享受。运动、饮食那些绝对连到它。吃对我是个挺干净的信号，或者零食是个挺干净的信号，至少对我像，好，我零食吃得比该多，而健康吃既能帮我识别我在那些点，也能就让我感觉更好。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: One thing I would say is that the therapist that I found, I found through a service that we had at Uber, and I think I was surprised how much stuff is covered by companies in terms of the ability to find a therapist, pay for a therapist or other tools. And so that's one thing I would suggest, go look through your benefits. Your healthcare provider offers a lot of that stuff too. So, those are a handful of. Listen to Lenny's podcast?
turns.zh: 我会说的一件事是，我找的那个 therapist，我通过 Uber 有的一个服务找的，而我觉得我惊讶于公司覆盖了多少东西——在找 therapist、付 therapist 或其他工具的能力上。所以那是我建议的一件事，去翻你的福利。你的医保提供商也提供很多那种。所以那些是一把。听 Lenny 的播客？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I hope that to be true. I don't know if that's anywhere near as powerful as these other things. One thing I'll mention is on the meditation front, there's this amazing book that kind of does exactly what you also describe where it teaches you why this works. It's called, it's kind of like a bad title, it's called Why Buddhism is True. And it's not trying to convince you to be a Buddhist, but it has a lot of incredible insights on why meditation is so powerful and how to think about it. So, I'll put that in the show notes too.
turns.zh: 我希望那是真的。我不知道那有没有接近这些别的东西那么有力。我会提的一件事是冥想前线上，有本超棒的书，基本做 exactly 你描述的——它教你为啥这 work。它叫，有点烂标题，叫《为什么佛教是真的》。它不是想劝你当佛教徒，但它有很多关于为啥冥想这么有力、怎么想的惊人洞察。所以我也放节目笔记。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Awesome.
turns.zh: 太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: I'm going to check that out.
turns.zh: 我要去查那个。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I wanted to come back to the burnout piece. I imagine some folks are listening to this and they're like, "Am I burnt out? I don't know." What are signs that you're burnt out versus just working a lot and tired?
turns.zh: 我想回到倦怠这块。我猜有些人在听这个、然后「我倦怠了吗？我不知道。」你倦怠 vs 只是工作多、累的信号是什么？

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: The one that I see the most is adaptability goes down really fast. And this is more me noticing I've managed a lot of people and coached a lot of people, so when I see that from people that I'm working with, I usually immediately bring up, I'm like, "Look, your openness to change in the business, or trying new things, or going back and trying things that maybe we tried before and didn't work has shifted from, 'Oh, here are the flags that we should be aware of, but let's give it a shot' to 'Why are we wasting our time? Let's not do this.'"
turns.zh: 我看到最多的是适应性掉得很快。而这更多是我注意到——我管过很多人、coach 过很多人，所以当我从共事的人看到那个，我通常立刻提，我像「看，你对生意里变化的敞开、或试新东西、或回去试之前试过不 work 的东西，从『哦，这是我们该注意的红旗，但试试看』变成了『我们为啥浪费时间？别做了。』」

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: This energy around, let's just do the thing we're supposed to do. And I think that's maybe specifically applicable to our environment, to high growth and marketing and product where it's just, that's just a key ingredient to doing this job well, is adaptability and flexibility and exploration. And if you're losing that, it's probably not because you've gotten bad at it, right? It's probably because you're just over it, right? Where you're like, "I just don't want to deal with the BS around this. I want to go do the thing that makes my job easier."
turns.zh: 这种「就做我们该做的那个事」的能量。而我觉得那也许特别适用我们的环境，高增和营销和产品，那里就是，那是把这份工作做好的关键配料，是适应性和灵活和探索。而如果你在丢那个，大概不是因为你变烂了，对吧？大概是因为你就是 over it，对吧？你像「我就是不想处理这周围的 BS。我想去做让我工作更容易的事。」

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Which again, most of the people that have chosen this career path want their jobs to be harder, because it's more fun, it's more interesting, it's more rewarding. And so when you're looking for ways to minimize the challenge or the opportunity, I think that's a pretty good signal that they may be more burnt out than just exhaustion. Because if anything, I see the opposite for people that are exhausted, where they get re-motivated by new stuff, by opportunities to go do something different and that kind of stuff.
turns.zh: 而再说一遍，大多选这条路的人想要他们工作更难，因为更有趣、更有意思、更有回报。所以当你在找方式最小化挑战或机会，我觉得那是个挺好的信号，他们可能更倦怠、而不只是 exhaustion。因为如果有什么，我看到 exhaustion 的人相反——他们被新东西、被去做不同事的机会重新激励。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. Really good insight. Second to last question, I know you have to run, where are you on this journey today and then just what's next for Adam Grenier?
turns.zh: 哇。真的好洞察。倒数第二个问题，我知道你得走了，你今天在这旅程的哪、然后 Adam Grenier 接下来啥？

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Yeah, thank you. Good question. I'm constantly optimizing this matrix of what am I good at versus what do I love doing? And so what I've found is that I really love entrepreneurs and working really closely with entrepreneurs and helping them figure out all of these funky things that I've been able to see over the last 20 years and maneuver. And I've worked at a lot of places and so I'm really good at context changing and helping connect the dots for people.
turns.zh: 对，谢谢。好问题。我一直在优化这个矩阵——我擅长什么 vs 我爱做什么？而我找到的是我真的爱创业者、跟创业者很紧密工作、帮他们搞清楚我这 20 年看到的这些诡异事、并 maneuver。而且我在很多地方工作过，所以我真擅长 context 改变、帮人连点。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: And so a couple ways I've found to be able to do that is advising companies, so working with founders and growth leaders and things like that and investing. And so I'm actually right now, I've been investing now for six, seven years. I've recently joined Andreessen's Scout fund, so I'm doing a bit more volume now. But I would say if I had to make a bet right now, I think a full-time or closer to full-time investing world is what I'd like to lean more towards. But I'm very much a let's just open up opportunities, and once the right one is in front of me, I'm going to tackle it.
turns.zh: 所以几种我发现能做那个的方式是顾问公司，所以跟创始人和增长领导那些工作、和投资。所以我现在，其实我投资现在六七年了。我最近加入了 Andreessen 的 Scout fund，所以我现在量更大点。但如果我现在得打赌，我觉得全职或更接近全职的投资世界是我更想靠向的。但我很「就让机会敞开，一旦对的在面前，我会搞定它」。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: And so who knows, I may go back full time somewhere or whatnot. But right now the advising, investing, coaching kind of hybrid is the term, I think it was Behzod at Reforge used, was me as a service is my current world. But I'd be shocked if I eventually don't gravitate towards some kind of foundation, because I thrive when I've got a little bit of an anchor.
turns.zh: 所以谁知道，我可能回哪全职，或啥。但现在顾问、投资、coach 的混合——术语，我想是 Reforge 的 Behzod 用的，是「me as a service」是我现在的世界。但如果我最后不 gravitation 向某种 foundation，我会震惊，因为当我有点锚时我 thrive。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. A mass, me as a service.
turns.zh: 惊人。一团，「me as a service」。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. For folks that may want to reach out to you about taking your money in their startup, or asking whatever questions, maybe advising questions, where can folks reach you and learn more?
turns.zh: 好。对可能想联系你、关于拿你钱投他们创业、或问不管什么问题、也许顾问问题的人，大家哪能联系你、学更多？

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Just Twitter, AKGrenier and LinkedIn as well, it's AKGrier. So, look me up, connect. I'm always open to connecting and chatting with people and I just love digging into problems. So, happy to abide.
turns.zh: 就 Twitter，AKGrenier，还有 LinkedIn，是 AKGrier。所以找我、连我。我一直敞开连人、跟人聊，而且我爱深挖问题。所以乐意 abide。

turns.en: Amazing. Adam, this was such an action packed chat, so many levels and layers. I can't wait for folks to listen to this. Thank you so much for joining me and being here.
turns.zh: 惊人。Adam，这是场信息量爆炸的聊，这么多层和维度。我等不及大家听这个。太谢谢你来、在这。

turns.speaker: Adam Grenier
turns.en: Yeah, thanks for having me.

turns.en: My pleasure. Thanks man.

turns.en: Good stuff. Take care.
